instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of “lobbyist” includes any individual who is employed by a principal or receives “economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses” and whose duties include lobbying, with no minimum dollar compensation amount stated.

The statute’s lobbyist definition and licensing restriction hinge on employment/economic consideration and (in some cases) days of lobbying communications, but do not set any lobbyist-side lobbying-expenditure dollar trigger for being a lobbyist.

Expense reporting duties in the provided text are imposed on principals (not lobbyists filing their own spending reports) and no per-item de minimis itemization threshold for lobbyist reports is stated.

A principal must register only after exceeding $500 in aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year, and principals anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and be exempt from licensing/registration/reporting if true.

Wisconsin’s de minimis in the lobbyist definition is based on at least 5 days of lobbying communications (not a percentage of compensated time), and no percent-of-time exemption from disclosure is specified in the provided provisions.
